description.en-US: Public repo for vpavlin Logos apps (QAKU + more).

summary.en-US: Local-first run tracker that syncs to your Basecamp over Logos

description.en-US: Perun records your runs (GPS route, pace, distance) on your phone and delivers them privately to the Perun Analytics module in your Logos Basecamp over Waku — no account, no server. Records with the screen off, and can run on the shared Logos Delivery node (toggle in Pairing).

summary.en-US: Local-first p2p zero-based budgeting on Logos

description.en-US:
KYM (Know Your Money) is a local-first, peer-to-peer zero-based budget you
own. Shared household budgets sync directly between devices over Waku — no
bank login, no server.

summary.en-US: The shared node your local-first apps grow in — one Waku node per phone

description.en-US:
Loam is the soil your Logos apps grow in: one shared liblogosdelivery (Waku) node per
phone, shared by every app over IPC — so ten apps don't each run ten radios. Per-app
consent, end-to-end encrypted (the service only ever moves sealed bytes), and an opt-in
offline cache that holds a closed app's messages so it reopens without re-syncing. It also
hosts a Bluetooth-LE mesh, so nearby phones can sync with no internet at all.

summary.en-US: The mycelial mesh VPN — your devices, no coordinator

description.en-US:
An encrypted overlay network between your own machines, with no coordination
server to trust or run. Nodes find each other through the network's own
gossip and move data directly between one another.

WireGuard carries the traffic. Peers find each other over Logos Messaging,
which is used only for rendezvous — once a tunnel exists it keeps working
whether or not the messaging network is reachable.

Addresses are derived from device keys, so there is nothing to allocate and
no address collisions. Peers that cannot reach each other directly fall back
to a relay, discovered from its own announcement rather than configured.

To join, scan the code that "shrooms invite" prints on a machine already on
the mesh. The invite is good for one device and fifteen minutes, and brings
back a membership credential signed for this phone's own keys. A network key
still works where there is no invite to scan.

Prototype.
